notes: The room is the owner's 7 by 4 pace shell from places/eliab_house.json, unchanged; the feast fills it and spills out through the RIGHT-wall doorway to the yard fire and the calf's fire (eliab_farm).
Asher sits on the north west stool, which faces the door, so from his seat the doorway frames the yard fire and the gate lamp, and from the gate (Sc 15) the robe shows through the door.
Amos's place is set and empty on the south west stool between Asher and Micah, so Micah speaks of the brother across it.
The drummer and the piper sit on the sleeping bench (BEHIND); the dancers' line weaves in through the doorway, up the table's east side to the hearth and back out to the yard fire.
Eliab brings the best of the calf in from the spit himself, sets it by the untouched bread and goes back into the dancing before the hearth, where Dan finds him in Sc 15.
The camera works from the table's open east side and leans an arm's length over the table for the close faces; the jars, stools and hand mill close the west side.
One long take of nine windows; its one hidden stitch is a dancer's mantle whirling past the lens (W04 to W05), and the rest continue.
It opens low among the stamping feet under the eaves and follows the bread in, and it ends in the doorway looking out past the fire to the gate lamp, the reverse of Amos's view in Sc 15.
The screenplay names only Asher, Eliab, Micah and the dog here, so the household and the neighbours stay unnamed, and an old neighbour eats on the north stool.
